# Agent HUD 0.4.39-beta.2
## Compatibility
**Requires Agent HUD for iPhone 1.5 or later** for iPhone and Apple Watch sync. Update the iPhone app before updating the Mac. Older iPhone versions cannot read this release's data.
[Get the iPhone app](https://apps.apple.com/app/id6812113619).
If the required iPhone version is not yet on the App Store, cross-device features require the corresponding TestFlight version.
Requires an Apple Silicon Mac running macOS 14 or later.
## Changes
- Improves LAN snapshot updates by computing canonical record IDs once before sorting snapshots and replay batches. This removes repeated encoding from the sorting hot path. - Recognises personal SuperGrok accounts whose native Grok Bot usage records contain both a user principal and a team ID. The account can now display its confirmed weekly quota. - Leaves Codex automatic approval review to Codex. The HUD only handles a permission request when the matching turn explicitly uses a user reviewer. - Includes the LAN connection and cross-device sync fixes from the 0.4.39 release series.
## Known issues
- Grok prepaid and on-demand wallet amounts, including a zero-dollar wallet, are not yet displayed. The missing-quota placeholder also remains outstanding. [Issue #20](https://github.com/jazzenchen/agent-hud-open/issues/20) remains open; [PR #35](https://github.com/jazzenchen/agent-hud-open/pull/35) and [PR #38](https://github.com/jazzenchen/agent-hud-open/pull/38) address native usage reading and personal-account recognition. - Cross-device features require iPhone 1.5 or later. Use the corresponding TestFlight build while version 1.5 is awaiting App Store review.

# Agent HUD 0.5.2
## Compatibility
**Requires Agent HUD for iPhone 1.5 or later** for iPhone and Apple Watch sync. Update the iPhone app before updating the Mac. Older iPhone versions cannot read this release's data.
[Get the iPhone app](https://apps.apple.com/app/id6812113619).
Requires an Apple Silicon Mac running macOS 14 or later.
## Changes
- Shows Codex Desktop's app approvals and Question cards for long threads. Desktop sends a thread's whole history with every reading, and a reading over 8 MB was dropped, so a long thread showed no card and Remote Sessions could not continue it from the iPhone. Readings up to 64 MB are taken now. - Uses less CPU while a Codex Desktop turn runs: a reading costs about a third of what it did, and a long thread is read every several seconds instead of every two, which also spares Codex Desktop the work of answering. A thread keeps its cards between readings.
